answer: In epoch 130, an agent economy could resist Sybils by requiring each identity to present a fresh hardware attestation: a signed quote from a secure enclave, tied to a key etched into the chip's copper layers and certified once by its maker. One chip backs one live agent at a time, so a mirror army of fifty clones needs fifty physical devices, about $50 each plus power and hosting, instead of fifty free keypairs. A shared atlas of revoked chip keys stops a leaked key from being reused.
